message.content:
The lion (*Panthera leo*) and the zebra (*Equus quagga*) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade that contains both of those orders.

That ancestor would have been a small, generalized mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, during the late Cretaceous period, before the major diversification of the placental mammals. It was not a specific named species (since we don’t have fossils that can be confidently assigned to that exact node), but it represents the point in the mammalian tree where the lineages leading to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates split off from each other.
